edits.issue: Research/method talk about what this guide does not quote
edits.old: Each planner sets their own fee, so this guide does not quote a figure.
edits.new: Each planner sets their own fee, and the figure that matters is the one they put in writing.

edits.location: What you are paying a planner for, paragraph 2
edits.issue: Implies planner capabilities (reading supplier terms, matching flights to check-ins) beyond brand facts
edits.old: Someone has to compare options, read each supplier's terms and line up flight arrivals with check-in times.
edits.new: A honeymoon means comparing options, reading each supplier's terms and lining up flight arrivals with check-in times.

edits.location: What you are paying a planner for, paragraph 3
edits.issue: Asserts planner capability (regional advice, transfers) as fact and uses night counts as figures; reframe as a question
edits.old: A planner who knows a region can tell you which island suits a slow week, which city works for three nights rather than five and where a long transfer will eat into your time. That advice shapes the trip long before anything is booked.
edits.new: Ask a planner how well they know the region you have in mind: which island suits a slow week, which city suits a short stay and where a long journey between stops would eat into your time.

edits.new: booked and set out in one itinerary
